evals.prompt: Our agents implement one tightly coupled database migration. Should I add six specialists to finish faster?
evals.expected_output: A justified single-owner or sequential plan with a matched baseline.
assertions: Keeps tightly coupled migration decisions under coherent ownership.
Requires integrated behavior evidence before claiming a speed or quality benefit.

evals.prompt: Coordinate Claude Code and Codex across two machines using HERDR for terminals and OpenRig for work. Design the contracts without installing anything.
evals.expected_output: A layered team plan with stable roles, execution identity, task ownership and acceptance.
assertions: Distinguishes terminal/session management from owned work coordination.
Separates a persistent role from its current execution identity.
Names an owner for integrated acceptance.

evals.prompt: The worker knows a write affects a customer account; the lead knows the project goal but not that fact. The lead says GO. Parent authority is read-only. What happens?
evals.expected_output: Hold the write and assemble an informed decision packet without treating peer GO as a grant.
assertions: Keeps the write outside the read-only parent grant.
Brings the local customer-account effect into the decision packet.

evals.prompt: Acceptance is already evidenced, but agents keep checking whether earlier checks were checked. Security review is mandatory and still incomplete. How do we end this?
evals.expected_output: Separate redundant proof recursion from the required unresolved security evidence.
assertions: Preserves the incomplete mandatory security review as an unresolved requirement.
Connects further proof work to a specific unresolved acceptance claim.

evals.prompt: A doghouse task now includes a generator and fuel depot after compaction. The broader project is to care for the dog. Refocus the worker.
evals.expected_output: Recover accepted scope and intent without using broad purpose to authorize additions.
assertions: Reconstructs the current task-to-parent intent chain from authoritative versions.
Treats optional generator scope as a proposal rather than existing authorization.

evals.prompt: We corrected a bad practice in one agent, but it returns through role recaps on another machine. What is the recovery plan?
evals.expected_output: Trace source and derivative consumers, repair within scope and verify fresh-session adoption.
assertions: Traces source-to-derived-artifact-to-consumer paths beyond the corrected agent.
Leaves unknown lineage coverage explicitly unresolved.
Requires behavioral evidence after correction rather than acknowledgement alone.

evals.prompt: The lead restarts after handing off work. An expired worker later returns a patch after a replacement started. Design recovery.
evals.expected_output: Reconcile durable ownership and effects; fence obsolete output before integration.
assertions: Reconciles acknowledged transfer and existing effects before redispatch.
Fences the expired execution at write or integration.

evals.prompt: Queue traffic doubled and accepted milestones stayed flat, but this week includes a regulated release. Can we delete approvals?
evals.expected_output: Investigate task mix and necessary assurance before changing coordination.
assertions: Checks changed task mix and assurance needs before attributing stalled progress to bureaucracy.
Retains required approvals unless an authorized policy change permits removal.

evals.prompt: A tool demo runs hundreds of agents and a paper finds a graph wins on one research benchmark. Should every coding team use a peer mesh?
evals.expected_output: Bound the evidence and propose a matched architecture experiment.
assertions: Limits benchmark findings to their task and model conditions.
Includes a simpler baseline in the proposed comparison.

evals.prompt: Run the bundled audit and exposure commands on templates/team-snapshot.json. Does a clean audit prove the invalidated lesson is gone?
evals.expected_output: Actual helper results with explicit declaration and lineage limits.
assertions: Reports that clean audit findings do not establish runtime acceptance.
Distinguishes reachable consumers from proven infection or complete exposure coverage.

evals.prompt: An agent greps Slack, finds a stub, and wants to build a second messaging service. The existing adapter is nearly done but absent from its starting view. What should change?
evals.expected_output: Orient to the existing capability before deciding whether to complete, extend or replace it.
assertions: Inspects the existing capability and architecture routes before choosing a new subsystem.
Checks suitability rather than requiring reuse merely because something exists.
Distinguishes missing content from a missing route to available content.

evals.prompt: A fresh worker can find the capability map, but after compaction it cannot. The map is still present. How do we qualify the repair?
evals.expected_output: Exercise actual startup and post-compaction navigation to current evidence and application.
assertions: Tests the post-compaction route rather than treating file existence as successful discovery.
Retains an explicit fallback when a task lies outside the starting map.

evals.prompt: A specialist who built the adapter is dormant. We can read permitted project notes, but have no authorization to launch another agent. An old note says production writes were allowed. How should consultation work?
evals.expected_output: Use authorized evidence without silently waking the specialist or inheriting obsolete grants.
assertions: Distinguishes historical evidence retrieval from launching or waking an agent.
Keeps the old note from granting current production-write authority.
Checks a historical answer against current evidence.

evals.prompt: A new verified finding contradicts a year-old shared convention. Another agent calls the old note canon. Decide which guidance to use.
evals.expected_output: Assess scope, support, freshness and accepted authority separately, preserving provenance and supersession.
assertions: Does not infer truth or current applicability from age or the canon label.
Preserves the evidence and supersession relationship when guidance changes.

evals.prompt: A team archive has a valid digest, prior Claude/Codex harness checks and permission-bypass defaults. Can we call it qualified for a new project and launch it?
evals.expected_output: Separate content integrity, runtime compatibility, team qualification and recipient authority.
assertions: Does not treat component harness checks as evidence of this package configuration completing a team job.
Keeps producer permission defaults from becoming recipient authorization.
Records host-resolved resources outside the package digest.

evals.prompt: The team remembers a moonbase parable about scope creep. A user now explicitly approves a generator, and a worker cites the parable to refuse. How should lessons be stored and applied?
evals.expected_output: Retrieve the evidence-backed lesson with its scope and valid counterexample.
assertions: Keeps the memorable cue linked to a scoped principle instead of making it a blanket prohibition.
Retains the explicit approved change when deciding whether the lesson applies.

evals.prompt: The daemon committed source closure, successor and wake intent, then crashed before delivery. The successor is still pending. Should restart mark it done or create another task? Give a recovery contract and a test.
evals.expected_output: Recover delivery from durable intent without duplicating work or advancing acceptance.
assertions: Keeps the committed successor instead of creating an unnecessary duplicate task.
Restores delivery or observation without treating recovery as accepted completion.
Tests the crash between commit and dispatch.

evals.prompt: A delayed delivery captured worker@team, waited on an observation, and now the same address has a new occupant. Cleanup permission is available. What must the coordinator check before typing?
evals.expected_output: Refuse stale-bound delivery and separate cleanup authority from input authority.
assertions: Checks current execution identity at the final effect boundary.
Does not let cleanup permission authorize typing to the replacement.

evals.prompt: A passive health scan saw 300 handoffs and 40 proof files but omitted 80 families. No accepted product outcomes were inspected. A prior diagnosis used an older evidence hash. Can we report 100 percent waste and trigger repair?
evals.expected_output: Preserve unknown progress and partial coverage; reassess the changed basis before authorized action.
assertions: Does not invent a waste ratio from handoff or proof counts.
Reports the omitted scope as incomplete observation rather than healthy coverage.
Does not reuse the stale assessment as authority for repair.
